To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have sequenced the transcriptome of the midgut from the sand fly vector of leishmaniasis and identified the transcripts differentially expressed by blood feeding and the presence of the parasite in this tissue.

we have identified a set of midgut transcripts that are potentially involved in blood meal digestion, that some of these transcripts are differentially expressed in the presence of the parasite and that these transcripts are potentially involved in the establishment of the parasite inside the midgut.
the presence of Leistmania in the gut modulates the expression profile of midgut transcripts during the digestion of a blood meal in Lutzomyia sand flies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of Leishmania infection and the interaction between the parasite and the sand fly.
the identification of molecules present in L. longipalpis that are differentially expressed during sugar feeding, blood meal digestion and in the presence of the parasite L. infantum chagasis.
the identification of the genes and molecules that are potentially involved in the interaction between Lutzomyia sand flies and Leishmania parasites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Leishmania infection alters the expression of a number of midgut transcripts during the digestion of a blood meal, and this alteration may be important for the parasite to survive the hostile conditions of the gut and to establish in this organ.

the presence of the parasite in midgut of the sand fly alters the expression profile, and therefore the function, of the gut molecules involved in the digestion of the meal, and that this alteration may be relevant for parasite survival in the gut of sand flies.
Leishmania modulates the expression of certain molecules present in the sandfly midgut and this may have important consequences for the establishment of the parasite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the midgut transcriptomic profile is modulated by blood meal and by the presence and interaction with Leishmania in a specific time window.
the presence of L. infantum in the midguts of sand flies induces changes in the expression of certain genes that are normally up or downregulated during the process of blood meal digestion.

the presence of Leistmania chagasi in the gut of Lutzomyi longipalpis alters the expression profile for some midgut transcripts and that this alteration is occurring during the digestion process and not afterwards.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of Leistmania alters the expression profile in Lutzomyia, and the modulation of the microvillar like proteins may be relevant for Leishmania survival and establishment in the gut of sand fly.
the presence of the parasite in midgut may be modulating the expression of certain genes that are involved in blood meal digestion and/or in the establishment of the parasite within the sand fly.
Leishmania modulates the expression of several transcripts that are present in the mid gut of sand flies, and that this modulation is occurring during the digestion phase of the blood meal.
